name: Dowelhasp
description: The rods cross at the belt with qi held in the hinge link, ready to launch any combination.

name: Brutal Roundstick
description: One rod strikes high and its twin follows low in a two-beat pattern against the same opponent.

name: Ducking Stickend
description: Turning on the hinge link as a center, the user slips half a pace to the outside of a lunge.

name: Guarding Capstick
description: A short upward hook of the rod catches a descending blow on its flat and rolls it away.

name: Savage Swingstick
description: The rod's side rakes down the opponent's wrist as the swing returns, loosening a weapon grip.

name: Keen Cascade
description: Three linked swings of alternating rods land on shoulder, ribs and thigh before the opponent can answer.

name: Ducking Tiedend
description: Stepping inside a swing, the user checks the opponent's arm with the taut link and slides past.

name: Rigid Octastick
description: A figure-eight ring of the rod before the chest keeps jabs and thrown scraps from reaching the user.

name: Grim Sidespin
description: The upward lobe of the figure-eight carries the rod into the underside of the opponent's forearm.

name: Grim Fliparound
description: The downward lobe drops the rod onto the opponent's lead hand or the top of the shoulder.

name: Rodzip
description: The feet follow the figure-eight's crossing point and carry the user to the opponent's open flank.

name: Whirrscreen
description: Reversing the eight's direction, the rod meets a thrust and flings it past the user's hip.

name: Rushing Hardstick
description: At the end of the figure-eight the rod's tail snaps across the opponent's wrist and stings.

name: Doughty Gripstick
description: Walking forward behind a ceaseless figure-eight, the user forces the opponent backward step by step.

name: Dowelscreen
description: The cord weaves through a crossing of the eight and closes around the opponent's forearm like a noose.

name: Acrid Neckwrap
description: The eight reverses abruptly so the rod rakes across a guard that was expecting the other direction.

name: Clackscreen
description: The free rod hangs low at the knee while the grip rod rests at the ribs, a guard that hides the reach.

name: Rough Hardstick
description: The wrist snaps and the free rod flies to the end of its cord, striking the opponent's near arm.

name: Lithe Chainjoint
description: The user steps in on the snap and out again on the recoil, never lingering within reach.

name: Padded Gripstick
description: The taut cord rests along the forearm and sends a descending stick sliding off toward the ground.

name: Rushing Backspin
description: A snap timed for the instant an opponent's guard lowers sends the tip over their forearms into the chest.

name: Clutching Shoulderroll
description: A flick of the cord at eye level makes the opponent flinch and lose sight of the rod's true path.

name: Sleet Capstick
description: A loop of cord is held open in the off hand while the rods guard the centerline.

name: Stamp Octastick
description: The loop drops over an advancing wrist and a pull of the rods draws it tight.

name: Brasswhirr
description: Letting the loop slide along the rod, the user releases the free end into a swinging blow.

name: Draught Cordjoint
description: Stepping through the opening of a raised loop, the user closes inside the opponent's reach.

name: Hazeclack
description: A rolling turn of the looped cord carries a weapon strike around the user and away.

name: Gagging Roundstick
description: The loop snags the opponent's elbow and a short pull spoils the swing they were beginning.

name: Clayrod
description: With the cord looped short, the grip rod's butt end jabs the opponent's ribs.

name: Sleetstave
description: Two loops close upon both of an opponent's forearms and are held taut, pinning them together.

name: Viselike Stickend
description: A loop on the wrist is hauled sharply downward, dragging the opponent's weight forward onto the front foot.

name: Galldowel
description: The loop catches a sword hilt or spear shaft and wrenches it out of the opponent's grip.

name: Rodbuckle
description: One rod rests in the elbow's crook and the other points ahead, a short guard from which transitions begin.

name: Ember Shoulderroll
description: The rod is carried to the elbow and thrown out again along the forearm, hitting at close range.

name: Emberstave
description: The rod passes behind the elbow to the other hand and swings from the opposite side.

name: Rillstave
description: As the rod changes hands, a long sliding step carries the user past the opponent's shoulder.

name: Haze Cordjoint
description: The rod rolls from wrist to elbow along the forearm, taking an incoming stroke on its length.

name: Sleet Tiedend
description: The free hand snatches the returning rod from the air and plants it before the face.

name: Cascade Scorer
description: The rod wheels from elbow to shoulder to hand in one turn, striking at three heights in sequence.

name: Poise Chainjoint
description: Passing the rod from shoulder to elbow, the user turns a blow aside and answers from below.

name: Sleetdowel
description: A held rod keeps a pulse of qi stored in the cord, ready to spring on contact.

name: Claywhirr
description: The rod strikes the opponent's guard, bounces off it and cuts around to the exposed side.

name: Haze Swingstick
description: A blow is knocked aside and the rod bounces off it directly into a rap on the attacker's wrist.

name: Clackcurl
description: Pushing off the rod's rebound, the user steps back a full pace, still facing forward.

name: Guarding Tiedend
description: The rods meet a heavy blow together and spring it away, saving the arms from its full weight.

name: Rushing Sidespin
description: The rod bounces from the ground and then the opponent's knee, finally returning to the user's palm.

name: Hum Neckwrap
description: A flick under the hilt of a weapon bounces it upward and loosens the wielder's grip.

name: Sprig Chainjoint
description: The rods tap an even beat before the chest, a moving guard that deflects any blow breaking in.

name: Stern Backspin
description: A swing from the left rod and then the right lands on opposite sides of the opponent's guard.

name: Crimson Octastick
description: Each hand strikes in turn at an even tempo, wearing down the opponent's forearm guard.

name: Clay Roundstick
description: The user's steps fall on the rods' beat, gliding in and out so the tempo hides the footwork.

name: Unmoving Cordjoint
description: A parry delivered one beat early or late turns the opponent's timed thrust aside.

name: Recall Fliparound
description: A half-speed tap lures the opponent's guard to move, and the real swing follows a heartbeat later.

name: Purpose Cascade
description: Alternating rods drum blow after blow on the opponent's guard until it begins to sag.

name: Grim Shoulderroll
description: A strike thrown between two beats of the pattern cracks the opponent's wrist before it moves.

name: Sidespin Barrier
description: A rod caught in the opponent's own rhythm is bound by the cord, throwing their attack out of time.

name: Brass Swingstick
description: Both rods are held tight to the ribs with elbows in, covering the body at inside range.

name: Crimson Fliparound
description: Gripping both rods, the user drives the cord-bar forward like a short punch into the opponent's chest.

name: Clackbuckle
description: The cord nips the crook of the opponent's elbow and the user turns, bending their arm out of line.

name: Neckwrap Swerve
description: A diagonal short step puts the user inside the opponent's weapon arm before it can extend.

name: Rill Hardstick
description: Pushing the taut bar outward, the user shoves a close thrust off its line.

name: Claystave
description: The cord bar drops to the hip and stops a kick or low strike against the thigh.

name: Rodscreen
description: The cord is laid across the opponent's arm and the rods pulled apart to lever it out.

name: Cruel Stickend
description: A tight spin of the short rod beside the user's own chest lands a blow at point-blank range.
